subject: Hospitality
title: Sustainability in Hotels
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sustainability in Hotels usable.

hook.text: Hotels consume enormous resources—a single guest uses 200+ liters of water daily. The industry is under pressure to change.

buildup.text: Green certifications like LEED and Green Key push hotels toward solar energy, water recycling, and waste reduction.

discovery.text: The 'reuse your towel' card was one of hospitality's first green moves in the 1990s. It saved millions in laundry costs.

twist.text: Critics call most hotel sustainability 'greenwashing'—small gestures that look good but don't address the real carbon footprint.

climax.text: Some hotels are genuinely net-zero. But the industry as a whole contributes about 1% of global carbon emissions.

punchline.text: Towel cards were the beginning. Real sustainability demands more.

quiz.question: What do critics call small hotel sustainability gestures?
options: Greenwashing—looks good but avoids real impact
